input.task: Which author has the most quotes listed on this page?

provenance: offline twin of task #3 of M10's SECOND held-out probe (docs/analysis.md §8a-2) — the repo calls the probe itself "probe #2" in verifier.py and its task "probe #3" in tasks/TODO.md, and this case's id follows the task numbering: 'which author has the most quotes listed on the first page?' came back `status: success, verdict: PASS` twice with two different WRONG answers ('Next →', 'Quotes to Scrape'). The first stub plan here is that same shape — one `extract` of the page heading — and it never runs: the plan lint rejects it before the first action and replans with a note naming the missing enumerating step. The second plan uses `extract_all`, the primitive M31 adds; the ranking is done in code (`verifier.rank`), never by the model. The runtime `verify()` call carries no ground truth, so `aggregate_needs_comparison` is what stands between this and a green run — it relaxes here because the trace really does contain the enumeration, which is the whole reason the guard could be relaxed at all. Ground truth: the fixture's author distribution is Albert Einstein 3, J.K. Rowling 2, one each for the rest. The fixture carries the real page's chrome links (Login, Tags, Next → — the last one is literally what the probe answered with), so `{role: link}` enumerates them alongside the authors and the counting branch has to survive them; it does here because each appears once. Two things this case does NOT prove, stated rather than implied: the counting branch is only robust to chrome that is rarer than the winner — a page whose pager text repeated four times would hand it a wrong winner — and the fixture does not reproduce probe #3's OTHER half, that on quotes.toscrape.com/js the authors carry no ARIA role for any plan to target (support-matrix D7, M32's subject).

triage.watched_red: before the lint and `extract_all` existed: checks {status: false, verdict: false, replans: false, actions: true}, status failure:semantic, answer 'Quotes Fixture' — the page heading, which is the probe's own failure shape (it answered with the page <title>) reproduced on a fixture. With the lint disabled but `extract_all` present, the first plan simply runs and the same wrong answer comes back, which is why the case pins `replans: 1`: the green run must go through the lint's replan, not around it.
triage.note: the green half of the M31 pair — `verifier-aggregate-superlative-fails-loud` is the red half. Both are needed: a lint that only ever rejects would be indistinguishable from deleting the capability. One limit of the harness, since the case reads as if it graded more than it does: `stub_planner` ignores the `note` argument entirely, so `replans: 1` proves the run went through the lint's replan path, not that the gap message is what closed the gap. Only the `full` suite, with a real planner, could grade the message itself.
